rationale_bullets: Underwood returns off a true-freshman season as the 2025 #1 overall recruit: 69.3 PFF/417 dropbacks (B10 +1 -> 70.3, ~p48), 2,428 yds at 60.3%, 11-9, plus 392 rush yds (PS).
The named 2025 context: 'limited by a conservative gameplan, plenty of drops from the receivers, but also rookie mistakes' (P6) - 9 INT, three sub-100-yard passing games, #12 B10 QB rating.

The scheme is the up-arg: Beck's power-spread is 'geared towards dual-threat quarterbacks, and Underwood's best games last year were the ones when he used his legs' (P6); Beck's Utah offense was the most-improved in FBS. PS: 'should be one of the Big Ten's top QB's.'
Coach-change noise is real (full staff import), but the QB room upgraded its floor: Fowler-Nicolosi (3,460 yds at CSU in 2023) is proven insurance.

60, M = the Maryland-Washington twin: near-identical mechanical read, higher pedigree, tailored scheme, minus transition noise. P6's own frame - 'Michigan's 2026 fate depends on Underwood's development' - is why confidence is M, not H.
data_gaps: No dated spring reporting on Underwood in the Beck install beyond books

rationale_bullets: Marshall returns as a proven All-B10 lead: 87.8 PFF/150 att (a whisker under the p90 RB reference of 87.9), 932 yds/10 TD with four straight 100-yard games in weeks 7-10 (P6/PS).

The room lost Haynes (81.1/121; 857 @ 7.1, OFY after USC) to Georgia Tech but signed the class's #1 RB, five-star Savion Hiter - 'should get carries right away and form a top duo with Marshall' (P6); 'looked the part in the spring' (PS).
Depth is real: Kuzdzal (70.9/76; the 20-100 Maryland game) withdrew from the portal and stays; Tatum (Oklahoma) adds pedigree; O'Meara/Ka'apana behind.
Context: RUN 87p / RBLK 85p as-played, and Beck's scheme just led FBS in yards/carry at Utah. PS: 'my #13 rated RB corps' (unit rank, attributed).
Weighted aggregate ~82 (~p72) on moderate samples + elite-recruit upside = 71, M.
Marsh is the proven piece: 75.8 PFF/288 routes (B10 -1 -> 74.8) as a TRUE FR - 45/651 all after September, B10 honors, 'an instant star' (P6).

GONE: McCulley (66.6/372; #2 at 588 yds - yr4), Morgan (55.7/163 -> UCLA), F.Moore (-> MSU), and BOTH TEs (Bredeson + Klein) - meaningful volume out of a room that already graded RECV 34th pctile with a national-leader drops problem (both books).

IN: Buchanan (64.2/277 at Utah, B12 +3 -> 67.2; '#5 receiver transfer' who started as a FR - P6), Top50 Ffrench (Texas; no meaningful volume), Top200 FR T.Johnson. TE: Z.Marshall (66.0/122, 16 rec) + Hansen.
P6's frame: 'a young room but has sky-high potential'; the Athlon scout lists Marsh/Ffrench/Buchanan among the reasons for excitement.
Weighted aggregate ~66.8 (~p52); the TE void and drops history hold it at 56, M - pedigree tail unpriced.

rationale_bullets: The import is a genuine star: Daley (92.0 PFF/513 at Utah, B12 +3 -> 95.0) - first-team All-American who LED THE NATION in sacks (11.5) until his Week-11 injury; 'should be back for fall camp' (P6). Utah's starting DT Lea'ea (66.1/623 -> 69.1) came with him.
The returning interior is credible: Pierce (72.9/405 -> 82.9; Athlon 'bullish'), Etta (62.7/295 -> 72.7; withdrew from the portal and stays), Nichols (72.2/198 -> 82.2), Brandt (59.2/405).

The outflow is heavy: both All-B10 linemen - D.Moore (89.9/440, rd-2 DET) and Benny (78.2/458, rd-7 BAL) - plus Guy/Payne/T.Williams and PFF-classed Barham (79.3/375). Five straight top-20 defenses set the program bar.
Blue-chip depth restock: four Top100 freshmen (T.Davis, Vallejo, N.Marshall) + five-star Carter Meadows.
Weighted adjusted aggregate ~78 (~p82) with four pieces at 72+; graded one notch under the mechanical for Daley's health dependency. 76, M - 'Whittingham always has a solid D-Line' (PS).
